Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

nonignorable 0.1.0

First release.

Screen

  • shadow_screen() reports, for each candidate shadow variable, its relevance for the outcome among the observed rows and its exclusion violation in the selection equation, both as incremental McFadden R². It has print() and plot() methods.
  • numeric = "classes" codes numeric characteristics as atom-free classes (screen_classes()) instead of linearly. Linear coding understates the exclusion violation when selection cuts hard on a characteristic.
  • The screen reports the cases of the rarer class per parameter of the outcome and of the response model (epp_relevance, epp_exclusion) and warns below 10, where extra parameters can manufacture relevance or violation.
  • A ratio whose exclusion chi2/df is below 1 divides by noise. The screen flags it in ratio_readable; print() names such candidates and plot() draws them hollow without a ratio.
  • A numeric outcome with more than two values is screened too: relevance comes from a proportional-odds model (MASS::polr) on outcome_classes classes of equal mass, five by default; a factor outcome with more than two levels by an ordinal (ordered factor) or a multinomial model (nnet). The screen measures relevance; it does not certify identification.
  • print() shows the verdict and its reasons in one column and fits 80 columns; plot() draws rejected candidates grey and labels them.
  • citation("nonignorable") lists the package and the two papers behind it.

Scan

  • sharp_scan() gives the sharp identified set for the rate of a binary outcome over a set of rows when the propensity ratio is at most exp(lambda): the average of eta(x), or, with unobserved = TRUE, the rows’ own missing outcomes, E(Y | R = 0). Rows are aggregated by "union" by default; "common" is available as an option.
  • sharp_scan_mean() gives the same for the mean of a non-binary outcome, also with unobserved, taking a grid of conditional quantiles. quantile_grid() builds that grid from a quantreg::rq fit, from any quantile function, or from draws.
  • sharp_scan_ci() adds a debiased estimate and a confidence set for the binary scan, with cross-fitted inputs from crossfit_inputs(). The standard error defaults to the larger of an empirical and a conditional one. It reports the rows with small r-hat and warns when the inverse weights blow up; crossfit_inputs() warns when the response model separates observed rows.
  • sharp_scan_mean_ci() adds a debiased estimate and a confidence set for the mean scan, for the mean over all rows, over a segment chosen by X, or of the missing outcomes. Its score is Neyman-orthogonal in both regimes of the cap, so no margin condition is needed. crossfit_quantiles() cross-fits the quantile grids and r-hat for any learner.
  • sharp_scan_contrast() compares two disjoint portfolios chosen by X, such as treatment arms. It gives the sharp set for the difference of their rates, a confidence set, and the selection strength from which “no difference” is no longer ruled out.
  • sharp_scan_mean_contrast() does the same for the difference of two portfolio means.
  • sharp_scan_ci() and sharp_scan_mean_ci() both target all rows by default. target = "unobserved" targets the missing outcomes themselves, E(Y | R = 0), such as the default rate of rejected applications, with the sharp set {psi - E(RY)} / pr(R = 0) and its influence function; a segment chosen by X restricts it. Both contrasts take among = "unobserved" to compare the missing outcomes of two segments.
  • sharp_scan_cdf() gives the sharp set for the distribution function P(Y <= t), or P(Y <= t | R = 0), at each value of a grid, with a debiased estimate and a confidence set pointwise in t; quantile() inverts the bounds into bounds for quantiles, widened outwards on the grid. The sets are sharp for each t, not as a band, and no uniform band is offered. The output reports the share of rows near the kink of each bound, where the normal approximation needs the margin condition. crossfit_cdf() fits P(Y <= t | R = 1, X) as one classification per t for any learner.
  • Debiased bounds and confidence sets are kept monotone in lambda.
  • The bounds without the cap pi <= 1 are called the outer band throughout (naive_* columns). Scans report the share of the rows entering the set where the cap binds and, for rates, the lambda from which it holds a bound flat; the plot notes such a bound in its legend, which it places clear of the curves, and leaves the flip labels a free strip below them. sharp_scan_mean_ci() counts rows with r-hat clipped below and above apart.
  • simulate_shadow(), obs_quantiles() and scan_inputs() provide data and inputs for examples and tests.
